title: Mixed level lowering
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $A\to B\to C$ be injective local maps of complete discrete valuation rings [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], with fraction fields $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ [def-pc-field-extension], and $M/L$ finite. Write $k_R=R/\mathfrak m_R$ for a residue field. Assume $\mathfrak m_AB=\mathfrak m_B$ and $\operatorname{char}(k_A)=p$. For any injective local map $R\to S$ of discrete valuation rings with fraction fields $E\subseteq Q$ and finite field extension $E'/E$, let $R'$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $E'$ and $S'$ that of $S$ in $(Q\otimes_E E')_{\mathrm{red}}$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Call $E'/E$ a weak solution if, for every maximal ideal $q$ of $S'$, its contraction $n$ in $R'$ is maximal, $R'_n,S'_q$ are discrete valuation rings, and $nS'_q=qS'_q$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Reduction is quotient by nilpotents; finite means finite-dimensional; local means pulling back the maximal ideal. For a finite extension $K_1/K$ put $A_1=\operatorname{IntCl}_{{K_1}}(A)$, $L_1=(L\otimes_KK_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, $M_1=(M\otimes_KK_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$, and let $B_1,C_1$ be the integral closures of $B,C$ in these reduced algebras [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. A finite separable extension is totally ramified with respect to a complete DVR when its integral closure is a DVR with unchanged residue field and ramification index equal to the field degree; the ramification index $e$ is defined by $\mathfrak m_R S=\mathfrak m_S^e$. A field extension is normal if every irreducible polynomial over the base with a root in the extension splits there. If $B$ contains a primitive $p$th root of unity $\zeta$, put $w=1-\zeta$ and $P(Z)=((1+wZ)^p-1)/w^p\in L[Z]$. For a degree-$p$ extension $M/L$ of mixed characteristic, finite level means that some generator $z$ has $\xi=P(z)\in L$ and $w^p\xi\in\mathfrak m_B$. Its level is the minimum of $\max(0,-v_B(P(z)))/v_B(w)$ over such generators with $P(z)\in L$, where $v_B$ is the integer valuation taking a uniformizer to $1$ (and $v_B(0)=+\infty$). Assume $\operatorname{char}(K)=0$, $B$ contains a primitive $p$th root of unity, $M/L$ has finite level $l>0$, and $k_A=\bigcap_{n\geq0}k_B^{p^n}$ inside $k_B$. There is a finite separable totally ramified $K_1/K$ such that either it is a weak solution for $A\to C$, or $L_1,M_1$ are fields, $\mathfrak m_{A_1}B_1=\mathfrak m_{B_1}$, and $M_1/L_1$ has finite level $l'\leq\max(0,l-1,2l-p)$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

source.place: Tag 09F5, lemma-lowering-the-level, including its definition of level immediately before the lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-epp-coefficient-constants-rigidity]. Thus $k_A$ is perfect and $\zeta\in A$, so $w,P$ are defined over $K$. Choose the common uniformizer $\pi$ of $A,B$, put $e=v_B(w)>0$, and choose a generator $z$ attaining the minimum level. Write $\xi=P(z)\in L$ and $n=-v_B(\xi)=el>0$. The finite-level condition and minimality give $n<pe$. Put $h=\max(0,l-1,2l-p)$ and $m=n-eh=\min(n,e,pe-n)$. These are integers with $m\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 09F5, opening and the definition of level preceding it; descent of the coefficient root by constants rigidity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-epp-truncated-pole-normal-form] with these $n,m,\xi$. In each alternative set $z_c=z+c+wzc$. The identity and estimates of [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-pole-calculus] give $P(z_c)=\eta:=\xi+P(c)+w^p\xi P(c)$ and $1+wc\ne0$. In alternative (i), $z_c$ still generates $M/L$. In alternative (ii), $z_c$ generates the base-changed algebra over $L_r$, since $z=(z_c-c)/(1+wc)$. In both alternatives $P(c)$ and $\eta$ have pole at most $n$, measured using $v(\pi)=1$. Apply [lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization] to $B\to C$: $C$ is the integral closure of $B$ in $M$, and is finite over $B$. Thus, in every subsequent base-changed algebra, integral closure from $C$ equals that from $B$: integrality over $B$ implies integrality over $C$, and the converse follows by transitivity since $C$ is integral over $B$.

source.place: Tag 09F5, reduction by translations and final uniformizer-root calculation.

proof.text: First take alternative (i). Minimality of $n$ implies $v_B(\eta)=-n$, so the displayed $a\in A$ is a unit. If $p\mid n$, perfectness gives $a=a_0^p+\pi a_1$ with $a_0,a_1\in A$. Put $b=-a_0\pi^{-n/p}$. Translate $z_c$ by $b$ once more. By [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-pole-calculus], the new parameter is congruent to $\eta+b^p-b$ modulo $\pi^{-n+m}B$. Its leading residue cancels, since in characteristic $p$ the residue of $(-a_0)^p$ equals $-\bar a$. Also $n/p<n$ and $m\geq1$. The new parameter therefore has valuation greater than $-n$, contradicting minimality. Consequently $p\nmid n$.

source.place: Tag 09F5, case J empty, minimality argument.

proof.text: Choose a root $y$ of $P(Y)=-\pi^{-n}a$ and set $K_1=K(y)$. The parameter has pole $n<pe$ and unit leading coefficient. By [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-branch-classification], $K_1/K$ is separable of degree $p$ and totally ramified. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-totally-ramified-base-change]: $L_1$ is a field and $B_1$ is a complete DVR weakly unramified over $A_1$. In the $\pi$-normalized valuation of $L_1$, the monic integral polynomial $P$ gives $v(y)=-n/p$: if $v(y)<0$ its leading term has strictly smallest valuation, and $v(y)\geq0$ would make $P(y)$ integral. Hence $1+wy\ne0$.

The element $z_c+y+wz_cy$ generates $M\otimes_KK_1$ over $L_1$. Its parameter is $\delta=\eta-\pi^{-n}a-w^p\eta\pi^{-n}a$. The first two terms differ by an element of $\pi^{-n+m}B_1$, and the last term has valuation at least $pe-2n\geq-n+m$ by [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-pole-calculus]. Thus $v_{B_1}(\delta)\geq-p(n-m)$ and $v_{B_1}(w)=pe$. Apply [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-branch-classification]. If the algebra splits, every normalized branch is $B_1$, giving a weak solution. Otherwise it is a degree-$p$ field extension, with finite level at most $p(n-m)/(pe)=h$. This proves the required alternative in case (i).

source.place: Tag 09F5, case J empty, final parameter estimate; Tag 09F3, normalized branches.

proof.text: Now take alternative (ii), and use its $K_r$ as $K_1$. Its stated degree and normalization show that it is finite separable totally ramified; $L_r$ is a field and $A_r\to B_r$ is weakly unramified. Write $q=p^r$. The translated parameter has pole at most $nq<peq$ and $v_r(w)=eq$. By [lem-sfb-epp-kummer-branch-classification], its algebra is split or a degree-$p$ field. If split, every normalized branch is $B_r$, giving a weak solution. In the field case with $v_r(\eta)\geq-(n-m)q$, its finite level is at most $(n-m)q/(eq)=h$. In the remaining case $p\mid d$ and the leading residue is not a $p$th power, so the same classification gives ramification index one over $B_r$, again a weak solution. The identification of integral closures in step 2 shows that these branch conclusions concern the stated $C_1$. In each weak-solution case, the maximal-ideal equality composes: $\mathfrak m_{A_1}C_{1,q}=\mathfrak m_{B_1}C_{1,q}=\mathfrak m_{C_{1,q}}$.

source.place: Tag 09F5, final paragraph, alternatives after telescoping; Tag 09F3 (C).

Item statement unchanged; it matches 09F5 (1)-(5) plus the completeness the parent supplies. Steps: (1) constants-rigidity gives k_A perfect and zeta in A; m=n-eh=min(n,e,pe-n)>=1, checked on small cases. (2) normal form at these n,m; group law; 1+wc!=0; lem-per-complete-dvr-finite-normalization's uniqueness clause makes C the integral closure of B, so IntCl(C,.)=IntCl(B_1,.). (3) minimality forces p not dividing n; the residue cancellation holds also for p=2. (4) the classification's p-not-dividing-d case makes K_1 totally ramified; the hypotheses of 09ER hold; v(y)=-n/p. (5) v_{B_1}(delta)>=-p(n-m), so split gives a weak solution and a field gives level<=h. (6) K_r: split gives a weak solution; the first valuation alternative gives level<=h; p|d with non-p-th-power residue gives index one and a weak solution. New nodes checked true: constants rigidity (finite intermediate field: index 1, residue field = k via the separable p^s-power argument, then 09E8), pole calculus (09F2 shape, v(p)=(p-1)e, valuation bounds), Kummer classification (unit 1+w^p eta, etale when eta integral, valuation of the root, U=t^{d/p}T reduction to U^p-a), truncated normal form (whole J-induction and root-adjunction calculus, including cross terms (p-1)e-n>=m-n and composition of translations).
